findings.title: Define r as distance from the sphere center in both languages
findings.baselineBasis: The frozen retained-source table explicitly requires center distance r >= R_0. The frozen independent model defines r as center distance and distinguishes sphere radius from an observation point's surface separation.
findings.observedCandidateDefect: Both complete modern drafts retain r >= R_0 and use r in the inverse-square formula, but neither defines r as distance from the center. EN prose[2] says: The source writes $r\geq R_0$; at the surface, the following expression means the limiting field approached from outside. ZH carries the same omission. The nearby point-charge-at-the-center sentence does not explicitly define the observation distance.
findings.impact: A reader can interpret distance from a sphere as separation from its surface and substitute that value for r in equation(8-16), producing an incorrect field and domain interpretation.
findings.requestedAffectedOnlyCorrection: In prose[2].text in both languages, explicitly define r as the observation point's distance from the sphere center, adjacent to the retained r >= R_0 condition. Keep the external one-sided surface-limit clarification. Do not change any formula, equation number, source_ref, figure object, task count or unrelated text.
findings.dependentUseNote: prose[7] uses r in equation(8-16), and prose[8] uses r < R_0. Their formula/inequality bytes need no change if the definition is restored at prose[2].
